## Conclusion

Next experiment if this were a real lab: Flow cytometry DNA-content + p-Histone H3 Ser10 and Aurora A/B target engagement to confirm polyploid endoreduplication vs mitotic arrest.

## PI review

Verdict: approve.

Top call Aurora over runner-ups supported by dose-orthogonal evidence: 1 uM (dose 4) independent clean profile shows massive large irregular nuclei (frac_large_nucleus z=+60.3, nuc_area z=+25.0, nuc_dna_integrated z=+21.5, form-factor/solidity strongly down) with preserved tubulin/actin, microscopy polyploid/lobulated nuclei, and 8/10 atlas neighbours Aurora mean similarity 0.894 (top 0.94-0.95). That discriminates vs protein synthesis (only high-dose 10 uM atlas signal, absent at cleaner 1 uM) and vs microtubule destabilizers (no tubulin depolymerisation, tub_mean z=-0.92, normal actin; combined atlas 5/5 split is expected mixing of toxic high dose and clean low dose). Direction same at 10 uM for irregular high-DNA nuclei, so not solely single-dose artefact though n=1/dose. Probability 0.85 is reasonable for Aurora kinase inhibitors.

## Unblinding

Compound: **AZ841** (PubChem CID [12001839](https://pubchem.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/compound/12001839))

Identity check: from the BBBC021 structure (the name is not in PubChem)

ChEMBL mechanisms: no curated mechanism in ChEMBL

## Verdict (computed by code)

Correct: agent said **Aurora kinase inhibitors**, BBBC021 annotates **Aurora kinase inhibitors**.

## Reflection

The correct call rested on the second acquisition choice at 1 uM. The 10 uM well showed irregular high-DNA nuclei but with low cell count, lower density and noisy actin texture, and its atlas match was 8/10 Protein synthesis. Dropping to 1 uM revealed the clean dose-stable signal: frac_large_nucleus z=+60.3 with form-factor and solidity strongly down and high DNA content, 559 cells measured, plus preserved tubulin/actin and microscopist polyploid/lobulated nuclei, with atlas 8/10 Aurora kinase inhibitors.

What misled was overweighting the high-dose atlas and the combined 5/5 Aurora versus Microtubule destabilizer split. This drove the interim split hypotheses of Aurora 0.40 versus Protein synthesis 0.35. In retrospect the high-dose protein synthesis signal was toxicity-related and the microtubule destabilizer signal lacked tubulin depolymerization support, but with n=1 per dose this required visual and cytoskeletal counter-evidence to discount.

The large-nucleus polyploidy phenotype is mechanistically consistent with Aurora inhibition causing cytokinesis failure and mitotic failure leading to polyploidization (PMID 20484572; PMID 39639371) and with Aurora inhibition inducing mitotic and cytokinetic defects (PMID 34406008).

What was right:
- Prioritized 1 uM clean profile with massive large irregular high-DNA nuclei (frac_large_nucleus z=+60.3, form-factor z=-39.2) over noisy 10 uM profile for Aurora call
- Used 1 uM atlas 8/10 Aurora plus microscopist polyploid/lobulated nuclei at both doses to outweigh high-dose 8/10 Protein synthesis atlas
- Rejected Microtubule destabilizers despite 5/5 combined atlas split because tubulin/actin were preserved with no depolymerization signal

What was wrong or missed:
- Overweighted 10 uM atlas 8/10 Protein synthesis in early hypotheses (Aurora 0.40 vs Protein synthesis 0.35) instead of immediately discounting low-count toxic high dose
- Combined-wells 5/5 Aurora/Microtubule destabilizer atlas was ambiguous and could have reopened destabilizers without cytoskeletal and visual checks
- Relied on n=1 per dose with density shift lower at 10 uM vs similar at 1 uM, leaving dose-dependence inferred from only two wells

Proposed next experiment: DNA-content flow cytometry across 0.3-3 uM AZ841 with p-Histone H3 Ser10 and Aurora B p-T232 to test for polyploid endoreduplication and Aurora target engagement versus mitotic arrest.
